texts: arrogance and downfall
need a doha about my boss who thinks he is better than everyone lol
O proud heart that swells and swaggers, crowned in its own applause and deaf to every voice but its own echo, sing me its folly.
I want a doha about a man who has grown so full of his own importance that he no longer listens to anyone, and who cannot see how small his constant boasting makes him.
My cousin got promoted last month and now he will not even say hello to the people he grew up with.
The blind man swears he sees it all, the moth is vain of its own bright dance, both rushing toward ruin; sing of swollen pride.
proud blind man, moth
My neighbour waves off every warning like a blind man striding ahead, then wonders why he keeps getting scorched, circling the same trouble like a moth.
Write a doha about the arrogance that makes a blind man swear he sees everything while a moth, vain of its own wings, flies straight into its end without once doubting itself.
can u give me a doha on a blind man bragging about his eyesight and a moth too proud to turn back
My friend topped the exams and now sneers at everyone who scored less, as if he was never a beginner himself.
self-important, looks down on all
Please give me a verse about people who walk into a room expecting the world to bow, who answer every kindness with a smirk, and who never imagine anyone else could matter as much as they do.
my uncle brags about his money at every wedding and nobody can stand it anymore
Oh the crown that only I can see, glittering on a head grown heavy with itself; sing the sorrow of that empty crown.
My sister corrects everyone at the dinner table and has never once admitted she might be wrong.
Give me a verse about the self-importance of people who think the whole world turns around them, who cannot hear advice, and who mistake their own noise for greatness and wisdom.
Swollen with the praise of strangers, he walks as though the earth were honoured by his steps; sing his vanity.
big talk, small man
ok so I want a doha about a guy who thinks he's the main character
honestly just a doha about people who won't admit they're wrong
Last week our manager took credit for the whole team's work and then gave a speech about his own brilliance.
I would like a couplet on the quiet fall that comes to those who strut and boast, who believe their name is carved above all others, and who forget that every proud walker eventually stumbles.
The loudest drum is hollow, and the proud man's laughter echoes in an empty hall; sing of that echo.
haughty, loud, doomed
Make me a doha about a rich man who spreads a fine cloth sheet over his seat and thinks that the fabric itself makes him taller than the villagers who stand before him.
cloth sheet, vanity
a doha about someone who is proud of his fancy cloth sheet pls
At my cousin's wedding the groom kept smoothing out his silk cloth sheet and glancing around to see who was admiring him.
Draped in a fine cloth sheet, he thinks the world should kneel; but the cloth is only cloth and the pride is only air.
Write a couplet for the proud man who boasts of his deep well of knowledge while the village weaver at his loom quietly makes real cloth that actually warms people.
He says his well is the deepest in the land, yet the weaver's loom keeps clicking on, making honest cloth, while he only makes noise.
well, weaver's loom, bragging
Our school's top debater keeps telling the quiet weaver's son at the loom nearby that his work is beneath him, but nobody drinks from the debater's well.
need something on pride, with a well and a weaver's loom in it, thanks
Our mill owner is so pleased with his oil press and his scent of success, like a musk deer that thinks the perfume is its own, that he looks past the labourers who keep it running.
hey, can you do a doha about a man proud of his oil press while a musk deer wanders by unaware of its own scent
oil press, musk deer, pride
Please compose a verse on how the owner of a great oil press brags of his wealth to everyone he meets, yet never notices the musk deer's fragrance he is proud of is not his own.
The musk deer boasts of no perfume, yet the proud man, grinding his oil press all day, brags of every drop.
Locked in his golden cage, the proud one believes he is the master of the whole sky.
I want a doha about the arrogant man living inside a cage he built himself, so pleased with its bars that he calls them the walls of a kingdom and refuses all advice from anyone.
cage, swagger, bragging
write something about a guy proud of his own cage lol
My father sits in his cage of rules and titles, certain that everyone outside it should answer to him.
Compose a verse about a musician who plays the one-string lute for crowds and grows so proud of the applause that he forgets the music was never really his own at all.
Pluck, pluck, goes the one-string lute, and the player thinks the whole world sways to him alone.
one-string lute, vain player
My friend learned a few songs on the one-string lute and now acts like the greatest singer the town has ever heard.
doha on a one-string lute player who's gotten too full of himself please
My brother buzzes like a bee around every party telling people how important his job is, loud and sure everyone is listening.
bee, buzzing boast
A doha for the man who hums with self-praise like a bee circling only his own hive, so busy announcing his greatness that he never hears what anyone else is saying around him.
short doha about a proud guy buzzing like a bee about himself
The bee drones of its own sweet honey, and the proud man drones louder still, drunk on the sound of his name.
can i get a doha about pride that grows like a seed?
I watched my nephew win one small award and now every sentence he speaks begins with how special he is, and that tiny seed of praise keeps sprouting.
pride's seed
A tiny seed of praise falls in the heart, and soon a towering vanity shades out every honest voice.
Write about how a single seed of flattery can take root in a person and grow, until they mistake their own greatness for the truth and cannot bear to hear any correction.
Who sits upon the throne of his own conceit, sees no guest at the gate, no friend in the crowd; sing his loneliness.
wanna doha about being too proud to ask for help
My old teammate would rather fail alone than let anyone see him struggle, because he cannot bear to look smaller than he pretends.
proud, alone, stubborn
Make me a couplet on the conceited person who insists he knows everything, brushes off every elder's counsel, and in the end finds nobody left to stand beside him when trouble comes.
Our neighbour keeps bragging about the rich scent of his rare perfume, though he is like a musk deer that thinks the perfume is its own work.
Compose a verse about a man who boasts he is the finest and most fragrant soul, while the musk deer carries its perfume without a word, and he never asks where his own fragrance truly comes from.
something about a musk deer and a boastful dude
The musk deer wanders unaware of its fragrance, and the boaster crows of a scent that was never his.
musk deer, empty boasting
washerman, bell, boasting
Every morning the washerman rings the bell at the ghat and struts as though the entire town depends on his shirt-scrubbing; he talks about it constantly.
doha on a washerman proud of ringing his bell all day?
Write a couplet about a washerman who rings a bell to announce how grand his work is, and who cannot stand being told that the dirt on other people's cloth is not his greatness.
The washerman rings his bell and swells as if the whole town bowed to him; sing the vanity of small bells.
Give me a verse for the proud who count the stars and name themselves greater than all of them, who tell every listener how bright they shine while forgetting the darkness they came out of.
stars, vain boast
My cousin was named employee of the month and acts like he is the brightest of all the stars in the office.
Under a thousand silent stars the proud man shouts his name, as though the sky would answer back.
doha about someone who thinks he outshines the stars
door, temple, proud
At the temple door he stands with his chest thrust out, announcing his giving, while the humble pass him unseen.
a doha on a guy who donates to the temple just to be seen at the door
I need a verse about the donor who stands at the temple door loudly counting every coin he gave, and who is so impressed by his own generosity that he never looks inside himself at all.
At the festival my aunt kept telling everyone at the temple door how much she had paid for the new gates, hoping they would all admire her.
Hey could you write a doha about someone proud of his cage and his bitter gourd, haha
The proud man sells bitter gourd and calls it honey, locked in a cage of his own praise.
cage, bitter gourd, arrogant
Write a doha about a vendor so conceited that he swears his bitter gourd is the sweetest in the land, locking himself in a cage of flattery and refusing to taste the truth of what he sells.
My chacha insists his bitter gourd curry is the best anyone has ever tasted, shut in a cage of his own certainty that nobody else knows how to cook.
I would love a doha about a young man whose success went to his head, who now speaks to his parents as though they were servants, and who thinks that being clever means he owes no one gratitude.
Puffed up like a festival drum, he beats his own praise, and none can hear the song beneath.
Ever since my friend got that big job abroad he talks down to the very people who helped him get there.
one on those who forget their roots after getting rich
vanity, proud, unbearable
proud of the well
Please give me a doha for the villager who is so proud of the well his grandfather dug that he refuses water to the thirsty, saying it belongs only to his family and that nobody else deserves a drop.
He peers into the well and sees only his own face, great and golden; sing of that reflection.
Our landlord shows off the old well in his yard to every visitor, though he never lets the poor children fetch even a pot from it.
i want a doha about a man guarding his well out of pride
A thousand gods may bless the poor, but the proud man blesses himself, over and over, till his voice is hoarse.
conceit, big words
Give me a verse about how pride makes a person deaf and blind to advice, so that even when everyone around him is trying to help, he waves them off and claims there is nothing left to learn.
My manager shot down five good ideas this week, then presented the sixth as if he had thought of it himself.
gimme a doha about someone who thinks they know it all
Even at the cremation ground the proud man arranges his seat of honour; sing his stubborn crown.
doha about a man who built a tomb for himself at the cremation ground just to show off
Write a couplet on the rich man who wants the grandest spot at the cremation ground, still ordering people about, still expecting the world to bow before his name even as his time is spent.
At my uncle's funeral the relatives kept arguing at the cremation ground over who deserved the front place, each insisting on their own importance.
cremation ground pride
sun-sized ego
My boss walks into every meeting as if the whole office orbits him, shining like the sun in his own certainty while the rest of us squint.
The sun does not announce itself, yet the small man shouts that he is bright; hear his hollow roar.
write a doha about a guy who thinks he's the sun
Compose a doha about the proud man who thinks everything revolves around him like the sun, and cannot see that the real sun shines on everyone equally without ever boasting of its glow.
The proud needle darts and boasts of every stitch it made, forgetting the hand that held it.
My tailor friend keeps saying the needle in his hand is the source of all his skill, as if the fabric and the customers meant nothing.
needle, vanity, boast
Give me a verse about a stitcher so vain over his work with the needle that he thinks the whole town depends on his hands, and who forgets the cloth never asked for his boasting.
doha pls about needle and big egos
I need a doha about a man who locks up his wealth and his advice from everyone, convinced he alone holds the key to wisdom, and cannot see that his lock keeps only himself out of friendship.
Proud one, you turn the lock of your own pride and lose the key in your own self-praise.
lock, pride, no key
doha on proud guy with a lock on his heart
My grandfather kept a lock on his strongbox and never let anyone touch it, convinced that nobody else could be trusted with a single thing he valued.
doha about a man who looks at himself in the mirror and then in the forest thinks all the trees bow to him
mirror, forest, vanity
Write a verse about the vain man who walks through the forest with a mirror in his hand, admiring his own face while the forest quietly carries on and does not notice his greatness at all.
In the forest's hush he holds up his mirror and bows to himself; sing the silence that does not answer.
My roommate spends an hour at the mirror every morning, then complains that the whole forest of people around him is jealous of his looks.
doha about a guy who's proud of his fancy cloth sheet
Make me a doha about the proud man who wraps himself in an expensive cloth sheet and looks down on the villagers, never realising the same plain weave that covers him will one day cover them all.
At the party my uncle kept adjusting his embroidered cloth sheet and scanning the room, waiting for compliments that never came.
Though the cloth sheet is woven of silk, it hides no emptiness; the proud man wears it like a crown.
cloth sheet, boasting
doha on a guy proud of his oil press by the river
The river runs past the oil press; the proud one talks of his mill as if he made the water too.
Compose a verse about a man who owns an oil press and sits above the river, swelling with importance as he counts every barrel, never noticing that the river flows past him without bowing once.
oil press, river, pride
The mill owner by the river walks his oil press like it's a throne, turning away the farmers who actually grew the seeds.
Whenever my father-in-law visits, he spends the whole evening telling stories where he is the hero and everyone else only listens.
On the stage of his own fancy, he is hero and king and audience; sing the lonely clapping.

Write a doha about the person who keeps reminding everyone of his past victories, who cannot enter a conversation without making it about himself, and who sees every other person as a mere audience for his story.
me, myself, mine
i want a doha on show-offs, you know the type
doha for the cloud that thought it was greater than the lamp
My colleague acts like a cloud heavy with rain, sure his presence will shade the lamp that others keep lit with their effort.
cloud, lamp, pride
Write a verse on how the swollen cloud boasts of covering the sky, yet cannot match the small lamp that quietly gives its glow, and how pride grows bigger than the things it claims to rule.
The proud cloud swells and darkens, scorning the little lamp, though it is the lamp that guides the wanderer.
He bought a new car and now narrates his own success to anyone, like a fish that cannot stop admiring its own shine.
fish, proud of itself
doha for a fish that thinks it's the king of the water
Write a verse about the little fish that leaps and glitters and tells the whole pond how great it is, forgetting that the water it floats in belongs to no one and cares not at all.
The fish leaps high, declaring himself lord of the waves, but the waves roll on without him.
doha on someone proud of their forehead mark
My aunt wears the tilak on her forehead every day and then lectures everyone about holier-than-thou, as if the mark makes her better than her neighbours.
I would like a couplet on the man who paints a fresh forehead mark every morning and parades before the village, sure that his show of holiness places him above everybody else.
forehead mark, show-off
A bright mark on the brow, a dark swagger in the heart; sing of the pride that dresses as piety.
The cleric's voice rises like a tower, and he looks down on every hearer, as if holiness were a throne.
doha on a cleric who thinks he knows God better than all
Our local cleric sneers at anyone who prays differently and insists that only he understands what God wants.
cleric, scholarly pride
Compose a verse about the learned cleric whose long speeches are meant not to teach but to show off, who delights in being called wise, and who cannot hear any doubt without anger.
doha about a guy bragging that he's captain of the boat
The boatman struts upon his deck as though he made the waves; the current hardly knows his name.
Please write a doha for the proud man who sits on his boat and orders everyone around, imagining he commands the current itself while the water simply carries him wherever it already wants to go.
boat captain's pride
The new team lead steers every meeting like it's his boat, forgetting the others are rowing too.
doha about a rich dude who bought out the whole inn just to show off
inn, proud guest
A guest of one night in a crowded inn, yet he orders the world as if the walls were his; sing his folly.
A man at the hotel kept ordering the staff around and boasting of his connections, though he was only there for the weekend.
I would love a doha about the visitor who stays one night at a roadside inn and acts like its master, bossing the servants and bragging about his rank to travellers who will never see him again.
doha about a guy so proud he wanted the fanciest bier
Upon the bier he is still proud, they say, for even there he demands a finer cloth; sing his stubborn crown.
Write a verse about the arrogant man whose followers carry his bier with all the old pomp, while he who once boasted that he was above everyone has nothing left to command.
At my uncle's last rites the family fought about how grand the bier should look, as if the dead man still needed to be admired.
bier, pride ends
Please give me a verse about the man who rubs sandalwood on his skin and drinks milk from a silver cup, admiring his own refinement while looking down on those who have neither of the two.
Sandalwood on his brow and milk in his cup, yet the heart beneath is bitter with pride.
My rich in-law bathes in milk and sandalwood and then talks down to our whole family, as if cleanliness were a talent.
sandalwood, milk, arrogance
doha about a man proud of his sandalwood and milk
My friend jokes that he only talks to people who are as smart as he is, and he really isn't joking.
Write a doha about the way a person who thinks too highly of himself turns away every offer of friendship, because he believes no one deserves to stand on the same ground as he does.
got a doha for a stuck-up person
A little man stands on a little hill, and cries that he has touched the sky.
self-importance, empty praise
doha about a doctor so full of pride he ignores the well that gives the village water
The village physician sits by the well and tells everyone how he alone knows the cures, never thanking the people who dug it.

Write a couplet about a physician who thinks his learning makes him better than the common people drawing water from the well, and who forgets that all his knowledge began with a simple question asked by a patient.
The physician boasts of his cures beside the well, yet the thirsty drink first and thank nobody.
well, physician, pride
The chakor bird gazes at the glowing night sky and thinks it is that bright itself; sing the pride that stares at far things.
My friend keeps posting photos with famous people and, like a chakor bird staring at what it adores, acts as if some of that glory is his.
chakor bird, proud gaze

Compose a verse about the chakor bird that gazes at the glowing night sky so long it begins to believe it is the glow, strutting about as though its devotion were glory and its watching were greatness.
a doha about the chakor bird that thinks it is as great as what it adores
He turns the lock against all counsel and fumbles his needle in the dark, too proud to ask for help.
lock, needle, pride
My grandfather will not let us help even when he cannot see to sew on a button; he keeps his needle under lock and key, because needing us feels like weakness.
Write a verse about the proud man who locks out all help and then tries to push a needle in the dark, too stubborn to ask anyone for a light, too vain to admit his hands are failing.
short doha on a proud old man with a lock and a needle
mosque, loud pride
Give me a verse about the man who prays loudly in the mosque so that all can hear his devotion, who feels a swelling in his chest as he counts the number of people watching him bow.
doha on someone showing off at the mosque
Within the mosque's silence he raises a showy voice; the Lord hears only the crowd's flattery.
At Eid prayers my neighbour kept glancing around the mosque to see who noticed how long he stayed in prostration.
My friend keeps saying his speech was the best of the evening, even though we all know he talks the way a rainbird screeches.
rainbird, loud boast
Write a doha about the rainbird who calls so loudly for the first drops that it believes it commands the clouds, forgetting that rain falls according to a will far greater than its own small cry.
The rainbird cries to the clouds as though its voice could bring the monsoon; sing the pride of a little song.
doha about a rainbird who thinks it summons the rain
Write a couplet for the king who surrounded himself with flatterers until he forgot that kings too are only people, and who believes all praise is simply the truth being told, never a favour paid.
When my grandfather's old business partner became wealthy, he stopped inviting us over and started inviting only those who flatter him.
The courtiers' praise is honey, and the king drinks until he can no longer tell his face from his name.
flattery, swollen head
doha on how praise goes to people's heads
He lifts his head so high that he never sees what lies beneath his own feet; sing his stumble.
doha about how pride always comes before a fall
A guy at work mocked the new intern for making errors, and the very next day he made the biggest one of the year in front of everyone.
pride, fall, folly
I want a doha that says the loudest boasters are often the first to fall, because they stop looking where they are walking and stop listening to the ones who might have warned them.
Our village headman sits under the old tree and boasts that the boat he has just bought is the finest, though he has never rowed one.
boat, tree, vanity
Write a doha about the man who sits under the shade of a tree and boasts of owning a boat, though he has never crossed the water, and who laughs at every real sailor who passes by.
doha about a guy bragging about his boat under a tree
Under a spreading tree he sails an imaginary boat, and calls himself captain of waters he fears.
The bee, drunk on its own honey, mistakes the philosopher's stone for a pebble; sing the pride that cannot see its fortune.
bee, philosopher's stone, pride
doha about a proud man who has a bee buzzing around his philosopher's stone and doesn't care
Compose a verse about the man who owns a philosopher's stone yet buzzes like a proud bee about his small honey, bragging about what he has made, never wondering what is truly priceless.
My neighbour has a talent that could change lives, but he swats everyone away like a bee and boasts of the philosopher's stone he thinks he found.
Compose a doha about the proud man who is dazzled by his own gold and thinks he floats above the world like a lotus, though his roots are in the same mud as everyone else.
He wears gold as a crown and thinks himself a lotus; yet the pond knows his roots are the same mud.
gold, lotus, proud
My rich cousin looks down on us with his heavy gold chain and calls himself above it all, as if he did not grow up in the same village.
doha on a gold-loving rich man who thinks he's a lotus above the mud

Compose a verse about the man who sits at his mirror each morning admiring his reflection and rehearsing speeches about his own greatness, who believes that if the world cannot see it, then the world must be blind.
Mirror, mirror, you flatter the one who stares too long; sing of the face that has forgotten the world.
My roommate checks his hair in every shiny surface and talks about how girls always notice him.
pls write about a vain guy and a mirror
mirror, vanity
leaf, forest, vain
doha about a leaf in the forest thinking it's the best of the leaves
One green leaf in the forest boasts of its shade, though the wind is already counting its days.
Write a verse about a single leaf in a vast forest that brags it is the greenest of all, forgetting the forest breathes through all its leaves together and that autumn will not ask its opinion.
My little niece thinks she is the greenest leaf in the whole family forest, and nobody can say otherwise.
